_about: Frozen interfaces for incord-code, written from the code AS IT IS (not as it might be). Checked by src/contracts.rs::check inside src/verify.rs on every task: a declared schema name must appear in some source file, and each of its fields must appear in a file that names the schema. Endpoint paths are matched by their route, method stripped. Matching is case- and punctuation-insensitive, so user_id / userId / UserId are one name. Types are recorded for readers; the checker does not interpret them.
_boundaries: Three processes: the harness (this crate, binary `incode`), the delegated agent (an installed CLI, spawned as a child), and the body (Incord Memory, HTTP on 127.0.0.1:9180). Everything under `endpoints` is a call this crate MAKES on the body; the crate serves no HTTP of its own.
_unnamed_shapes: Three wire shapes cross the boundary with no named type in the code — the enqueue card body, a decision-history row, and a handoff item. They are built or read field-by-field out of serde_json::Value. Declaring invented names for them would fail the check (measured: it did), so their fields are recorded under the relevant endpoint as `_request_fields` / `_response_row_fields` / `_response_item_fields`. Those keys are kept and ignored by the parser, so they are documentation and NOT enforced. Giving them real structs would make them enforceable; that is a code change, not a spec change.

ProjectBrief._owner: src/brief.rs — the body's brief for one project. The intake gate reads it; nothing here stores it.

fields.goals: string — what the proxy should protect
fields.synopsis: string — the PRD in a few lines; rides every review prompt

RoadmapItem._owner: src/brief.rs — one item of the ordered plan. `status` is compared case-insensitively; anything that is not `done` reads as open.

fields.title: string — must name a heading or a numbered section of the PRD, or it counts as untraceable scope

BriefUpdate._owner: src/brief.rs — what `save_brief` writes back. A field left absent keeps its current value; it is never cleared.

fields.endpoints: Endpoint[] — or an object with a `routes` list; both are parsed

fields.fields: map<string, string> — or a list of {wire|name|field, type}; both are parsed. Anything else is an ERROR, never an empty set.

fields.path: string, e.g. `POST /api/users`; may also arrive split as {method, route}
fields.response: string — the name of a declared schema

Task._owner: src/ledger.rs — one unit of execution. `state` reaches `done` through Ledger::complete alone, which cannot be called without a Verified.

fields.roadmap_id: string — the roadmap item this implements; the ledger is not a second plan
fields.title: string
fields.verify: string[] — argv of the check that settles this task
fields.evidence: string — the recorded command summary that closed it
fields.contracts: string[] — the schema names this task must honour
fields.est_tier: string — which role/model tier the work is estimated at
fields.worked_by: string — the agent identity that attempted it, never the model
fields.owner_note: string — a `change` verdict's instruction, carried to the next pass

TaskState._owner: src/ledger.rs — seven states, serialised snake_case. There is deliberately no `failed`: a failure is an attempts counter and a note.

fields.pending: in the ledger; dependencies not all done
fields.done: verified by a passing command; terminal
fields.abandoned: out of attempts; not retried without a person

CommandEvidence._owner: src/verify.rs — what running a check actually produced. Fields are PRIVATE and only `run` constructs one, so proof cannot be minted for a command that never ran.

fields.exit: i32? — None means killed or timed out, which is a failure and never a pass

Guards._owner: src/guards.rs — extra protected paths beyond DEFAULT_PROTECTED, set once by a human.

fields.protected_paths: string[] — matched against the workspace-relative path with forward slashes

AdminConfig._owner: src/admin.rs — one settings file. Every value can say which layer decided it.

fields.roles: map<string, string[]> — role name to ordered model candidates
fields.verify_command: string[]? — beats detection, loses to INCORD_VERIFY_CMD

Plugins._owner: src/admin.rs — which body-facing readers are switched on.

Ticket._owner: src/owner.rs — the receipt for a raised card. No token means no answer can ever be read, which is an error and not a success.

Verdict._owner: src/owner.rs — what came back. Five verbs, matching the service. An unrecognised verb is an ERROR and is never read as approval.

fields.decided: bool — false is a real answer meaning `not yet`, not a failure
fields.verb: string enum: approve | change | dismiss | hold | info
fields.by: string — who decided; the owner or the proxy, never conflated
fields.note: string — `change` only: the instruction the next pass must read

Hit._owner: src/recall.rs — one compact ranked match. Previews only; full content costs a second call.

Ref._owner: src/recall.rs — the pair that identifies one stored message.

Finding._owner: src/auditor.rs — read-only. The auditor owns the findings lifecycle; a second trail here would be a copy that disagrees.

fields.severity: u32 — MEASURED to arrive as a string on the live payload; both forms are accepted
fields.summary: string — taken from rounds[0].text, the auditor's first statement

TurnOutcome._owner: src/agent/mod.rs — how one delegated turn ended.
TurnOutcome._crosses: harness <- agent CLI (child process, stream-json on stdout)

fields.served_by: string[] — the models actually BILLED. Empty means `not reported`, never `none`.

TokenUsage._owner: src/runtime/usage.rs — cumulative for a turn; what the budget counts.

RateLimitInfo._owner: src/agent/claude_code.rs — subscription quota, reported instead of a dollar figure. Wire names are camelCase; the Rust names are snake_case via serde rename.

fields.status: string — `allowed` is the only value that means work can proceed

ToolStatus._owner: src/tools/tool_status.rs — whether an external binary is installed, cached so every session does not re-probe the PATH.

SpecFile._owner: src/spec.rs — one document of the spec set. Every entry must have a named consumer; a file nothing reads is cost, not documentation.

fields.consumer: string — the role in the loop that reads it, or the owner

endpoints._note: Returns the WHOLE ProxyConfig — briefs plus the owner's rules, mode, model and severity ceiling. Treated as opaque JSON and patched at one path.
errors: connection refused — the body is not running; the gate reports this rather than assuming an empty brief
non-2xx — `the service answered <status>`
timeout after 5s — a slow answer before the first prompt is indistinguishable from a hung start

endpoints._note: REPLACES the whole document. A partial struct posted here would silently delete the owner's rules. Read back after writing; `it returned ok` is not evidence the field landed.
errors: the config has no `briefs` list
`briefs` is not a list
a brief needs a project name
the brief was written but could not be read back

_request_fields.title: string — required; the match key for a reusable past verdict
_request_fields.severity: u8 — clamped 1..=5 by the service; decides whether a closed phone is buzzed
_request_fields.source: string — always `guard`, so the proxy will not auto-decide the card

errors: a card with no title is rejected by the service
the card was accepted without a token, so no answer can be read
the verdict did not parse
the verdict `<verb>` is not one this harness knows how to act on — never read as approval

endpoints._note: Query: limit. Reply carries `decided`, a list of rows. Only consumed `approve` / `dismiss` rows are reusable.

_response_row_fields._why_not_a_schema: read field-by-field out of serde_json::Value; there is no named row type in the code
_response_row_fields.title: string — matched EXACTLY; a differently phrased question is a different question
_response_row_fields.project: string — compared by suffix, never by `contains`
_response_row_fields.consumed: bool — an unconsumed row is not an answer

errors: the history did not parse

endpoints._note: Query: query, top_k. Returns always-on rules unioned with the ones matching the turn, so they ride the turn rather than the system prompt.
errors: unreachable body — the turn proceeds without rules rather than failing
unreachable body
malformed response
unreachable body
malformed response

endpoints._note: Body: {text, kind, subject}. Reply carries isError / content[0].text / stored / msg_id.
errors: isError true — reported as the tool's error, never swallowed
no `matches` array — read as no results, not as a failure

endpoints._note: Correction path. Body carries {confirmed}; the reply carries confirmation_required / deleted / idx.
errors: confirmation_required — a preview, not a deletion; never auto-confirmed

endpoints._note: Query: task=<absolute workspace path>. Reply carries `items`. Nothing is cached here; the recorder lives in the body.

_response_item_fields._why_not_a_schema: read field-by-field out of serde_json::Value; there is no named item type in the code
_response_item_fields.name: string — the tool name; an item without one is skipped
_response_item_fields.observations: u64 — how many times it was witnessed

errors: unreachable body
no `items` array — read as nothing solved yet
the auditor's answer did not parse
no `findings` array — read as no findings, not as a failure

endpoints._note: The body's standing guard categories. Reply carries rules[].key, rules[].always and forward_all. Read once at session start, 4s budget.
errors: unreachable body — DEFAULT_PROTECTED still applies, so the guard never silently opens
